title: Hot Springs: the Arlington Hotel with Joe Caprero
summary: He doubled clarinet, saxes and flute at the Arlington Hotel in Hot Springs in a dance band and under Mr. Grosso's concert ensemble.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: So you've been on the flute quite a few years.
Yeah, I played, I worked in Hot Springs and I played with the Concert Ensemble and played flute there.
You playing with the jazz band too?
Also, yeah. I doubled clarinet, alto, tenor, bass-axe and flute. And it was a very easy job at the Arlington Hotel. We worked a total of eleven hours a week.
I bet that was Joe Caprero's band.

Yeah, I was in a dance band with Joe Caprero but the Concert Ensemble was under Mr. Grosso. But the men that played with Joe had to double with him. You see, three nights a week you played in the lobby of the hotel and you played concert, and then the other three nights a week you played the dance in the ballroom.
Do you remember approximately? I was in 19, I was in 19, I was in 19, I went to New York in 1936, or that's when I came back, that was around 1939 or 1940.
A pretty big band at Caprero?
Yeah, well he had three saxes and three brass, standard, you know, and bass and drums, and he played guitar himself and piano.
